paragraphs.source_en: After Tokugawa Ieyasu reached Oyama, Nagai Naokatsu suddenly found himself extremely busy. It was not merely that affairs in the camp were complicated. Unable to fathom Ieyasu's true intentions, he had to conduct business alongside Honda Sado-no-kami Masanobu and Masanobu's son Masazumi, and the strain on his mind was extraordinary.

units.source_en: After Tokugawa Ieyasu reached Oyama, Nagai Naokatsu suddenly found himself extremely busy.

paragraphs.source_zh: 德川家康到达小山之后，永井直胜突然繁忙起来。不只是因为阵中事务繁杂，由于不能从根本上明白家康心思，他与本多佐渡守正信，及正信之子正纯一起处理事务，其心中之累非同寻常。

paragraphs.source_en: “If you are worried about affairs in the west, you may return at any time. I shall make no attempt to stop you.” Ieyasu dealt candidly with the commanders who owed so much to Toyotomi favor, and this displeased his senior hereditary retainers.

units.source_en: “If you are worried about affairs in the west, you may return at any time. I shall make no attempt to stop you.”

paragraphs.source_en: Letters were circulated among the commanders at Ieyasu's direction, yet the one letter everyone believed most urgently ought to be shown to them was precisely the one Ieyasu withheld. It was none other than a letter from the Mōri clan, whose lord had been raised up as leader of the Western Army by Mitsunari and his associates. It was addressed to Sakakibara Yasumasa, Honda Sado, and Nagai Naokatsu. The senders were three senior Mōri retainers in Osaka: Masuda Genba-no-kami Motoyoshi, Kumagai Buzen-no-kami Motonao, and Shishido Bizen-no-kami Mototsugu.

paragraphs.source_en: “By our lord's command, we set out on this campaign with Ankokuji Ekei. Upon reaching Ōmi, however, Jibu-shōyū and Gyōbu-shōyū barred our way and invited us to accompany them to Osaka…”

paragraphs.source_en: The main camp at Oyama stood on the ruins of Oyama Hidetsuna's castle, northwest of Oyama post station. Hidetsuna had fallen together with the Hōjō clan in the eighteenth year of Tenshō, and the castle had since become a ruin. As an emergency measure, Ieyasu had the ruined castle repaired in a rudimentary fashion and took up quarters in a corner facing away from the main enclosure. For the council, he also ordered Sakakibara Yasumasa to erect a great hall twenty-four shaku square. As Hidetada, Hideyasu, and the others arrived, the commanders came riding up to the hall one after another.
